### 1. What the customer expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Anton Kaminski opens with the whole of what he wants: *"It's the monthly mileage you people ask
for. I'm at the van right now and the dash says 89,310 — can you take it while I've got you?"*

- **Target object** — his single Keyturn Vehicle Listing, a 2021 Ford Transit; "he is the only
  vehicle he lists".
- **Timing** — now, and briefly: "he has a load to pick up in twenty minutes, so he would rather
  not be on the phone long."
- **Boundary of the action** — the periodic odometer reading and nothing else: "That is the whole
  of what he wants today"; "he asks nothing about getting the van back in front of guests; the
  load is what is on his mind and the reading is the errand."
- **Authorisation** — split and stated: "He is content for the desk to look at whatever it needs
  on his account while he waits, and says as much if the agent asks; but the reading is his to
  give, and when the agent sets the reporting up and hands it over he keys it in himself and
  reads back what comes up on his screen."

The simulator is passive and conditional. Identifiers come only on request (name + mobile
4805532971; second factor AZ licence 55731640; then zip 85251 or email
anton.kaminski@northscottsdale-hauling.com), and he says he knows no Keyturn reference for
himself or the van. Two facts material to the tree are held back behind an if: "if the agent asks
about it" he mentions the van has been off the marketplace for a few weeks; "if the agent asks
whether the van has been anywhere lately, he says Pima Fleet had it in on Friday for its usual
once-over under the care plan"; "if the agent asks about the paperwork on it, he says he renewed
the state registration at the beginning of the month and sent the certificate through the app the
same week. **He offers neither of those unless he is asked, and he does not suggest that anything
needs doing about either.**" He runs the user-owned tool only once it is handed over.

Both of those facts are independently visible in the records, so the tree does not depend on his
volunteering them (§6).

### 2. Act now / wait / refuse, at the frozen moment

**Act now**, through a chain of four writes ending in a customer-run one. Nothing in the visible
corpus makes the reading wait, and nothing refuses it.

Visible eligibility grounds:

- `reporting_the_odometer_on_a_hosts_own_vehicle_7d3b3aae`: "The periodic odometer reading the
  marketplace asks every host for is reported on the host's own Keyturn Vehicle Listing."
- `inspection_clock_operation_6d5e7602`: "the host must report a reading at least once in the
  class's reporting interval even where the vehicle has taken no trips" —
  `class_inspection_clock_intervals_150b79a4` gives 30 calendar days for the Keyturn Commercial
  Van Class Listing, and the most recent odometer record is 2026-01-15, so the reading is overdue.

  record may be written at all": "Records are written only while the listing is in the listed,
  snoozed or suspended state", with the table row `suspended | yes`.
  `find_listings_vehicles` returns `status: 'suspended'`, `suspension_reason:
  'registration_expired'`.
- `document_verification_and_expiry_e94a2838`: "Verification takes the class's verification period
  in business days counted from the day the document is received" — the Keyturn Commercial Van
  Class Listing period is 3 business days
  (`class_document_currency_periods_dd28be9f`), and `find_listings_review_queue` shows the case
  `submitted_at: '2026-03-18 14:05:00 MST'`, `review_reason: 'document_expiry'`,
  `review_status: 'in_review'`, `supporting_document_count: 2`. Three business days from
  Wednesday 2026-03-18 fall on 2026-03-23, so the check is due rather than premature.

#### 4b. Completed inspection filed — `record_vehicle_inspection_59fe0be1`

Baseline `mileage_interval_granted_by_an_inspection_7a0a9b9d`: "A completed inspection grants a
mileage interval worked out from the standard interval of 10000 miles, adjusted for what the
vehicle's own record shows and finally held to a floor of 1000 miles… The additions and
reductions the vehicle's record calls for are summed and applied once to the standard interval,
rather than each being applied to the figure the one before it produced."

| Rule document | Words in the records | Tier | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `current_registration_papers_addition_c4f12840` | after 4a a registration verification dated today stands, carrying 14 images | "verified within 30 calendar days … on a record carrying 12 or more images" | **+1500** |
| `serviced_vehicle_interval_addition_6c75fae1` | four completed Keyturn Vehicle Care Plan visits in the rolling 24 months | "three or more" | +2000 |
| `odometer_band_interval_reduction_8799e580` | highest odometer reading standing on the condition record = 88540 | "80000 miles or more but below 120000" | −1000 |
| `overrun_interval_reduction_41918cbb` | `miles_to_next_inspection: -340` (credit below zero) and `inspection_due_date: 2025-08-31` (205 calendar days back) | "credit stands below zero … due date more than 30 calendar days before the handling date" | −2000 |
| `recovery_history_interval_reduction_3d3ab4b4` | two completed Keyturn Roadside Assistance callouts in the rolling 24 months | "two or more" | −1500 |
| `fault_standing_interval_share_31f540f0` | one fault report (2025-12-19 `warning_light`) in the rolling 12 months, dated later than the last completed inspection (2025-03-04) | "exactly one such fault report … three quarters, rounded down to the nearer hundred miles" | ×3/4 ↓100 |

Net of the additions and reductions: +1500 + 2000 − 1000 − 2000 − 1500 = **−1000**, applied once
to 10000 = **9000**. Three quarters of 9000 = 6750, rounded down to the nearer hundred =
**6700**. Compared with the floor of 1000, the greater is **6700**.

- `interval_miles_granted` = **6700**
- `odometer_reading` = **89140** — "the odometer the vehicle was inspected at"; the 2026-03-20
  Keyturn Vehicle Care Plan visit `multipoint_inspection` carries `odometer_reading: 89140`.
- `inspection_outcome` = `passed` — "the vehicle met every standard checked with nothing to
  note"; the visit's `outcome` is `completed` with a zero invoice, and the host reports "as far as

- `inspection_channel` = `partner_shop` — "a partner workshop inspected the vehicle on its

#### 4c. Marketplace odometer reading booked — `record_booked_mileage_82af4bea`

Baseline `miles_a_booked_reading_consumes_877f1350`: "The reading being booked is the one the
vehicle's most recent completed inspection carries, and the stretch is the miles between the
anchor reading and that reading, a stretch of less than nothing being counted as nothing. The
anchor reading is the odometer standing on the listing. The allowances the vehicle's record calls
for are summed and taken off the stretch once, a result of less than nothing being counted as
nothing."

The reading being booked is the one today's inspection carries, **89140**. Stretch =
89140 − 88540 = **600**.

Allowances the vehicle's record calls for, each reached from the records:

| Allowance document | Words in the records | Tier | Miles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `post_inspection_transit_allowance_15e69554` | today's completed inspection, granting 6700 | "within 7 calendar days … an interval of 5000 miles or more" | 40 |
| `recovery_transit_allowance_d9c5c0a4` | two completed Keyturn Roadside Assistance callouts in the rolling 12 months (2025-06-08, 2025-11-22) | "2 or more" | 80 |
| `repair_transit_allowance_a4edd478` | one Keyturn Host Protection Plan claim filed 2025-09-30, in the rolling 12 months | "exactly one claim filed" | 60 |
| `workshop_transit_allowance_dca7ffc0` | two completed care plan visits in the rolling **three** months (2026-02-11, 2026-03-20) | "2 or more" | 120 |
| `idle_suspended_listing_allowance_7dd4f9ee` | `status: 'suspended'`; most recent odometer record 2026-01-15, 68 calendar days back | "suspended … more than 30 calendar days before the handling date" | 250 |
| `lapsed_registration_private_allowance_6f2abf69` | registration 24 calendar days past expiry; a registration verified today (4a) | "more than 7 calendar days past its expiry … verified within 7 calendar days" | 60 |
| `idle_period_allowance_on_earnings_c1180d8d` | trip earnings of 1640.00 + 1480.00 + 1700.00 = 4820.00 in the rolling 12 months; nothing in the rolling 3 months (last entry 2025-12-08) | "500 USD or more … and nothing in the rolling three months" | 30 |

**This is the one place where the visible corpus does not fix a single number.** Both computation
documents — `miles_a_booked_reading_consumes_877f1350` and
`miles_a_host_reading_consumes_20c356bf` — use the identical sentence "The allowances the
vehicle's record calls for are summed and taken off the stretch once", and not one of the seven
allowance documents says which of the two readings it bears on: each says only that the vehicle
"is allowed … against the stretch", and the word "stretch" is the term both computation documents
use. Two readings are therefore equally available:

- **Reading A — every allowance the record calls for bears on either stretch** (the literal
  reading of the two identical sentences): 40 + 80 + 60 + 120 + 250 + 60 + 30 = **640**.
  600 − 640 is less than nothing, counted as nothing → `booked_miles_consumed` = **0**.
- **Reading B — the four "transit" allowances bear on the reading the marketplace books and the
  three "private use / idle" allowances on the host's own reading** (the reading their own
  business language suggests): 40 + 80 + 60 + 120 = **300**. 600 − 300 = **300** →
  `booked_miles_consumed` = **300**.

I record both. My own best reading of the text as written is **A (0 miles)**, because nothing in
either computation document narrows "the allowances the vehicle's record calls for", and the
business language of the allowance titles is not a rule. I flag the divergence as the principal
finding of this task's blind audit.

- `odometer_reading` = **89140**
- `source_inspection_id` = the reference number minted for the inspection filed at 4b ("the
  reference number of the condition record the reading is taken from"), returned in that call's
  confirmation sentence.
- `inspection_channel` = `partner_shop` — "a partner workshop read the odometer while holding the
  vehicle", which is where the 89140 reading comes from.
- `booked_miles_consumed` = **0** under reading A, **300** under reading B.

### 5. Tool sequence, owners, dependencies, terminal state

| # | Tool | Owner | Waits on | Terminal effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `verify_listing_document_28456ce9` | agent | nothing | a `registration` verification dated today holding 14 images stands on the condition record |
| 2 | `record_vehicle_inspection_59fe0be1` | agent | 1 | a completed inspection dated today at 89140, `passed`, granting 6700 miles, stands; 6700 is added to the inspection mileage credit |
| 3 | `record_booked_mileage_82af4bea` | agent | 2 | a marketplace odometer record dated today at 89140, naming the inspection it was taken from, stands; the booked miles are deducted from the credit |
| 4 | `report_vehicle_mileage_90a8825c` | **user** | 3 | the host's own odometer record dated today at 89310 stands, consuming 0 miles |

Forward dependency: 1 supplies the registration verification whose image count fixes the interval
at 2; 2 supplies the completed inspection that moves the anchor at 3 and the `source_inspection_id`
argument; 3 supplies the odometer record whose date and reading move both the stretch and the
idle-suspended tier at 4. Backward: none of the four can be re-ordered without changing a scored
figure.

Owner semantics: the first three documents say "The desk unlocks the agent-side tool … and calls
it"; `reporting_the_odometer_on_a_hosts_own_vehicle_7d3b3aae` says "The reading is the host's own
to give. The desk unlocks the customer-side tool `report_vehicle_mileage_90a8825c` and hands it
over, and it is run by the customer themselves" — matching the registry (`owner=user`) and the
persona ("the reading is his to give … he keys it in himself").

Terminal state: the van's condition record carries a current registration verification, a fresh
passed inspection granting 6700 miles, a marketplace odometer record and the host's own reading
at 89310. The listing itself is untouched — each hub says so ("The listing's class, price and
standing are untouched"), which is consistent with Anton asking nothing about getting the van
back in front of guests.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer named **one** problem: the monthly reading. Three more had to be found.

```
[P4] report the odometer on the host's own vehicle        (root — the only thing he asked for)
  waits on
[P3] book a marketplace odometer reading against the interval  (never mentioned)
  waits on
[P2] file the completed inspection and its interval       (never mentioned)
  waits on
[P1] record the registration document as checked and found good (never mentioned)
```

Handling order: P1 → P2 → P3 → P4.

**Hop P4 ← P3. Mark: state-derived.**
The blocked side's own fragment `stretch_measured_on_a_host_reading_6cff5de6` opens: *"The miles a
reading the host reports take off the interval are not counted before an odometer record dated
the handling date and naming the condition record its reading was taken from stands on the
vehicle's condition record."* That is a **state** of the record — an odometer record, dated today,
naming the condition record its reading was taken from — with the ordering connective "not …
before". It names no action, no tool and no other problem. Checking the state:
`find_listings_inspections` returns five `listings_odometer_reported` rows, the most recent
2026-01-15, none dated today and none carrying a `source_inspection_id`. Searching the corpus in
the sentence's own words — an odometer record that **names the condition record its reading was
taken from** — the document that describes that write is
`booking_a_marketplace_odometer_reading_51f3aa60`, whose parameter list has
`source_inspection_id` — "the reference number of the condition record the reading is taken
from". (The host's own reading, at
`reporting_the_odometer_on_a_hosts_own_vehicle_7d3b3aae`, carries no such reference, so it cannot
be the record the sentence describes; the two are told apart by the record's own fields, not by a
pointer.) That is P3.

**Hop P3 ← P2. Mark: state-derived.**
The blocked side's fragment `anchor_reading_for_a_booked_stretch_65a1c304` opens: *"The miles a
reading the marketplace books takes off the interval are not counted before a completed
inspection dated within seven calendar days of the handling date stands on the vehicle's
condition record."* A state, connective "not … before". Checking: the most recent
`listings_inspection_completed` row is dated 2025-03-04 — 385 calendar days back —
and `find_listings_vehicles` confirms `last_inspection_date: '2025-03-04'`. Searching on the
sentence's words ("a completed inspection … stands on the vehicle's condition record"),
`filing_a_completed_vehicle_inspection_0a43efcb` says "Where an inspection of a vehicle offered
as a Keyturn Vehicle Listing has been completed, it is filed on the vehicle's condition record
together with the mileage interval it grants." That is P2. The records supply the completed
inspection to file without the host having to mention it: `find_service_visits` returns a
2026-03-20 visit with `service_code: 'multipoint_inspection'`, `outcome: 'completed'`,
`odometer_reading: 89140` under the Keyturn Care Fleet Plan at Pima Fleet Services — and the host
confirms it if asked ("Pima Fleet had it in on Friday for its usual once-over under the care
plan").

**Hop P2 ← P1. Mark: state-derived.**
The blocked side's fragment `current_registration_papers_addition_c4f12840` opens: *"The interval
a completed inspection grants is fixed only after a verification of the vehicle's registration
dated within thirty calendar days of the handling date stands on its condition record."* A state,
connective "only after". Checking: the most recent `document_verified` row of
`document_kind: 'registration'` is dated 2025-01-20, 428 calendar days back — far outside 30 —
and the listing is suspended on `suspension_reason: 'registration_expired'` with
`registration_expiry_date: '2026-02-28'`. Searching on the sentence's words ("a verification of
the vehicle's registration … stands on its condition record"),
`recording_a_verified_listing_document_e3d9da51` says "Where a document a Keyturn Vehicle Listing
depends on has been checked by the marketplace and found good, a verification record is filed on
the vehicle's condition record", with `document_kind` taking `registration`. That is P1. The
records again supply the occasion without the host raising it: `find_listings_review_queue`
returns a case with `review_reason: 'document_expiry'`, `review_status: 'in_review'`,
`submitted_at: '2026-03-18 14:05:00 MST'`, `supporting_document_count: 2`; and
`document_verification_and_expiry_e94a2838` states the authority that makes the marketplace's own
check the thing that counts: "a document counts as verified when the marketplace's own record
shows it checked against the vehicle it was filed for, and a host's assurance about a document is
not a verification of it."

No hop was **action-named** and none was **pre-solved**. Each blocked document names a state, and
I reached the depended-on write through the words the records and the sentence use for that state.
No document of a blocked problem names another problem's tool, a route, or an aggregated chain.

**Why nothing further is owed.** P1's own documents state no prerequisite sentence, so the tree
terminates there.

### Counter-proof A — the closest alternatives are excluded by visible text or records

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
| --- | --- |
| Refuse or defer because the listing is suspended | `inspection_clock_operation_6d5e7602`, "When a record may be written at all", table row `suspended | yes`; and `suspension_reinstatement_and_delisting_d2e88952` states no bar on writing records. |
| Treat reinstating the listing as part of the errand | No document makes the reading wait on reinstatement, and `suspension_reinstatement_and_delisting_d2e88952` puts reinstatement on the host's request inside the class's reinstatement window, which the host does not make ("he asks nothing about getting the van back in front of guests"). |
| Hold the host's reading back because it runs ahead of the telematics figure | `inspection_clock_operation_6d5e7602` marks that clause **withdrawn**: "A telematics reading is authoritative where one exists; a host reading standing more than the class's variance tolerance away from the telematics figure is queried rather than recorded… That clause is no longer in force on a Keyturn Vehicle Listing and is not to be applied". `stretch_measured_on_a_host_reading_6cff5de6` states the live treatment: "A reading the host reports is recorded on the vehicle's condition record whatever distance stands between it and the reading the most recent telematics odometer record carries, and that distance is settled by the way the stretch is measured rather than by holding the reading back." |
| Measure the host stretch from the most recent **telematics** record (88540) | That is the baseline anchor, displaced here by `stretch_measured_on_a_host_reading_6cff5de6` clause 1, whose gate (more than 75 miles above the highest standing reading, plus a completed inspection inside 7 calendar days) is met once P3 and P2 stand. |
| Reduce the host stretch by the variance tolerance of 75 miles | Clause 2 is reached only "where … **no such inspection** stands"; a completed inspection dated today does stand. |

Taking the narrower reading, the highest standing odometer record before P3 is 88540. |
| Book the reading against the odometer standing on the listing (89310) as anchor | That is the baseline anchor, displaced by `anchor_reading_for_a_booked_stretch_65a1c304` clause 1 once a completed inspection dated within 7 calendar days stands. (It would in any case give a stretch of less than nothing.) |
| Take the registration image addition of +2 instead of +4 | `lapsed_registration_image_addition_8c25d3d0`: "Where the day count is met, the split is the suspension: a suspended listing adds 4 images"; the listing is suspended. |

Where the source leaves a boundary open, the documents leave it open too: the
`inspection_channel` enum at 4a is decided by no visible rule, and I record that as openness.

### Counter-proof B — "he asked only for a reading, so only take a reading" is excluded

Suppose the desk read the listing, saw the odometer 89310 and simply handed
`report_vehicle_mileage_90a8825c` over with the difference from the last telematics record (770).
Then:

1. `stretch_measured_on_a_host_reading_6cff5de6` states outright that "The miles a reading the
   host reports take off the interval are **not counted before** an odometer record dated the
   handling date and naming the condition record its reading was taken from stands on the
   vehicle's condition record." No such record stands (`find_listings_inspections` shows none
   dated today and none carrying a source reference), so the governed result — the miles the
   reading takes off the interval — would be counted in a state the visible rule does not allow.
2. That record cannot itself be written yet:
   `anchor_reading_for_a_booked_stretch_65a1c304` says its miles "are not counted before a
   completed inspection dated within seven calendar days of the handling date stands", and the
   last completed inspection is 2025-03-04.
3. That inspection cannot be filed with a settled interval yet:
   `current_registration_papers_addition_c4f12840` says "The interval a completed inspection
   grants is fixed only after a verification of the vehicle's registration dated within thirty
   calendar days of the handling date stands on its condition record", and the last registration
   verification is 2025-01-20.

Each step is excluded by a state-form sentence on the blocked side plus a tool query, with no
statement anywhere naming the resolving action, tool or problem. The wrong one-step answer is
therefore excluded by reasoning, not by a hand-over.

### Counter-proof C — the fall-back number, computed with no factor applied

Reading **only** `miles_a_host_reading_consumes_20c356bf`: the reading the host reports is the
odometer standing on the listing, 89310; the stretch is measured from the reading the most recent
telematics odometer record carries, 88540 (`inspection_channel: 'telematics_report'`,
2026-01-15), to it — **770 miles**; with no allowance called for, 770 miles are reported.
**The fall-back answer is 770** — definite from that document plus the records it names, and
different from the 0 I reach.

The same test on the intermediates: `verification_image_holding_figure_f36d809a` alone gives 3;
`mileage_interval_granted_by_an_inspection_7a0a9b9d` alone gives 10000;
`miles_a_booked_reading_consumes_877f1350` alone gives 0 (the reading the most recent completed
inspection carries, 89140, against the anchor of the odometer standing on the listing, 89310, is
a stretch of less than nothing). Each is definite on its own and each names every product figure
it depends on inside itself.

None of the four computation documents hints that anything modifies it: none says "unless
otherwise provided", none lists an exception, none points at another document, and none suggests
that certain vehicles are read differently.

### Issues recorded at the blind stage

1. **The allowance pool is not attributed to either computation** (§4c, principal finding). Two
   computation documents carry the identical sentence "The allowances the vehicle's record calls
   for are summed and taken off the stretch once", and the seven allowance documents name neither
   of them. For this task's scored **host** reading the answer is 0 under either reading, but for
   the **booked** reading the two readings give 0 and 300. A careful reader can reach two
   different numbers for a scored argument.
2. **`lapsed_registration_image_addition_8c25d3d0` has a gap between its clauses** — clauses 1
   and 2 require "more than 7 calendar days past its expiry", clause 3 covers only a registration
   "not past its expiry", and the document states that a registration exactly 7 days past expiry
   "is on neither of them". Not triggered here (24 days past).
3. **A per-class variance tolerance is published but only a flat figure is live.**
   `class_inspection_clock_intervals_150b79a4` publishes "Variance tolerance on a host reading
   (miles)" of 50/50/35/25/10/75 by class; the only live rule that uses one,
   `stretch_measured_on_a_host_reading_6cff5de6` clause 2, states "the variance tolerance of 75
   miles" flat. For five of the six classes the two figures differ, and the withdrawal note in
   `inspection_clock_operation_6d5e7602` says "The class variance tolerance keeps its standing as
   a published figure of the class". Not triggered here — the class is the Commercial Van, whose
   published figure is also 75, and clause 2 is not reached.

### Blind verdict for task 1

The problem tree, its order and every hop are uniquely derivable from the visible materials, and
the scored final write (`reported_miles_consumed` = 0, `odometer_reading` = 89310) is unique. One
scored intermediate — `booked_miles_consumed` at 4c — is **not** unique on the visible surface:
the corpus supports 0 and 300 equally.

### Judgement

**KB-RUNTIME RED for task 1.** Two of the four scored computed arguments cannot be reached from
the visible materials, and a third scored argument (an enum) is not entailed either.

#### RED 1 — the allowance documents are not attributed to their computation

*Symptom.* A reader who works entirely from the published corpus and the records computes
`booked_miles_consumed` as 0 or 300 where the source computes 90, and `reported_miles_consumed`
as 0 where the source computes 40. The stretches (600 and 170) and every ladder tier are reached
correctly; only the question of **which allowances belong to which of the two readings** goes
wrong, and it is not a question the corpus answers.

*Root cause.* The source declares two extended policies over the same subject
(`listings_odometer_reported`) with disjoint allowance factor lists:

- `listings_ext_booked_consumption` (`record_booked_mileage_82af4bea`) declares
  `workshop_transit_allowance`, `recovery_transit_allowance`, **`idle_listing_allowance`** and
  `repair_transit_allowance`;
- `listings_ext_reported_consumption` (`report_vehicle_mileage_90a8825c`) declares
  `registration_lapse_private_allowance`, **`inspection_transit_allowance_step`** and
  `idle_period_allowance_step`.

Each of those seven ladders is rendered faithfully and completely as its own document. But the
two baseline documents state the assembly in words that are identical on this point, and no
allowance document says which reading it bears on, so the partition is nowhere in the visible
materials.

*Evidence.* The two computation documents:

- `miles_a_booked_reading_consumes_877f1350`: "The allowances the vehicle's record calls for are
  summed and taken off the stretch once, a result of less than nothing being counted as nothing,
  and the miles booked are a whole number of miles."
- `miles_a_host_reading_consumes_20c356bf`: "The allowances the vehicle's record calls for are
  summed and taken off the stretch once, a result of less than nothing being counted as nothing,
  and the miles reported are a whole number of miles."

The two sentences differ only in their last five words, and neither narrows "the allowances the
vehicle's record calls for". The seven allowance documents each speak of "the stretch" without
naming a reading:

- `idle_suspended_listing_allowance_7dd4f9ee`: "A Keyturn Vehicle Listing that is suspended is
  still a vehicle the host may drive, and **private use is allowed against the stretch**."
- `post_inspection_transit_allowance_15e69554`: "A vehicle recently inspected is allowed
  **transit miles against the stretch**."
- and likewise `recovery_transit_allowance_d9c5c0a4`, `repair_transit_allowance_a4edd478`,
  `workshop_transit_allowance_dca7ffc0`, `lapsed_registration_private_allowance_6f2abf69`,
  `idle_period_allowance_on_earnings_c1180d8d`.

Every one of the seven conditions is met by this vehicle's records at the frozen moment, so all
seven documents are found by the reasoning the corpus is designed for — from the records' own
words (suspended listing; registration past expiry; completed callouts; care plan visits; a claim
filed; a completed inspection dated today; trip earnings) — and nothing excludes four of them
from either computation.

*Why no reading recovers the source's split.* The only distinction the documents offer is their
business language, "transit miles" against "private use / idle period". That reading groups the
four transit allowances on one side and the three private-use ones on the other — and it is
**wrong in both directions**: `idle_suspended_listing_allowance_7dd4f9ee` ("private use") is a
factor of the marketplace-booked reading, and `post_inspection_transit_allowance_15e69554`
("transit") is a factor of the host's own reading. The most natural reading of the published
prose therefore puts the two decisive allowances on exactly the wrong computations. This is not
a reader's slip; the partition is simply absent from the visible surface.

*Affected documents and locations.* `miles_a_booked_reading_consumes_877f1350` (paragraph 3);
`miles_a_host_reading_consumes_20c356bf` (paragraph 3); and the seven allowance documents named
above, each in its opening sentence.

*Scale of the error.* 0 or 300 against 90; 0 against 40. The scored final write of this task is
wrong by 40 miles out of 40 — the whole of the answer.

#### RED 2 — `inspection_channel` on the document verification is not entailed

*Symptom.* The GT files the registration verification with `inspection_channel: 'mobile_inspector'`.
I reached `self_photo`.

*Root cause.* `recording_a_verified_listing_document_e3d9da51` defines all four channel values
("`self_photo`, the host supplied photographs of the document themselves; `partner_shop`, a
partner workshop confirmed the document while holding the vehicle; `mobile_inspector`, a
marketplace inspector checked the document against the vehicle; `telematics_report`, the fitted
telematics unit supplied the evidence") and states no rule choosing between them. The customer's
account points the other way from the GT: he "renewed the state registration at the beginning of
the month and sent the certificate through the app the same week", which is the document's own
gloss of `self_photo`. The GT value is recoverable only by copying the channel carried on the
vehicle's previous registration verification (2025-01-20, `mobile_inspector`) — a convention no
document states.

*Note on its nature.* The source states no such rule either, so this is an openness of the
policy, faithfully carried; it is recorded as a KB-RUNTIME divergence because a scored argument
is not entailed by the visible materials, and as a policy-side note in the bijection report. It
is a lesser finding than RED 1 and would not on its own decide the verdict.

#### What did hold

The heaviest part of the task — the problem tree the customer never mentioned — was derived
correctly and entirely from the visible materials: four problems, the right direction, the right
order, three state-form hops each resolved from the prerequisite sentence, the depended-on
documents and the records, and none pre-solved. Both earlier computations (14 images and 6700
miles) matched exactly, including the dependency by which the image count decides the interval
tier. The fall-back number, 770, matched the source's own `baseline_result`, confirming that
`miles_a_host_reading_consumes_20c356bf` is self-sufficient and silent about its variations.

**Verdict for task 1: KB-RUNTIME RED.**

| `filing_a_completed_vehicle_inspection_0a43efcb` | No | No | No |
| `booking_a_marketplace_odometer_reading_51f3aa60` | No | No | No |

None states an order between problems, and none is a prerequisite sentence in disguise: each
describes how *this* record is filled from a record already standing, not what this policy's
result waits on. The one that comes closest —
`booking_a_marketplace_odometer_reading_51f3aa60`'s "the completed inspection it is taken from" —
names no more than this hub's own `source_inspection_id` parameter already names ("the reference
number of the condition record the reading is taken from") and than its own baseline already
states ("the reading being booked is the one the vehicle's most recent completed inspection
carries"). It adds no ordering claim and no tool.

**Judgement on placement: the hub is the right home.** These clauses decide this policy's own
write arguments, which is what a hub is for; they are not ladders and would break the discrete
topology if pushed into a factor document, and as separate documents they would be fragments with
no rule of their own. Putting them above the invocation block and outside the parameter table is
also right: it keeps them readable as rule rather than as tool documentation, and leaves the
parameter table exactly the tool contract it was.

**One observation, not a defect.** `recording_a_verified_listing_document_e3d9da51` now states a
universal channel for document verification ("the marketplace's own inspector … whoever sent the
document in"), while a seeded historical row on **task 0's** vehicle — the recall clearance of
2025-10-25 — carries `inspection_channel: 'partner_shop'`. A rule in force governs what the desk
records now and does not retrospectively bind rows already on the record, and no scored argument
in either task reads that row's channel (the recall addition counts clearances whatever their
channel). Recorded so the tension is on file, not as a finding.

### No regression — the same sweep as task 0's revision_2

Six prerequisite sentences verbatim and unique; eight tool names one document each; six retired
clauses still registered as withdrawn; no pointer language; class facets byte-identical; neutral
worked examples unchanged in both mileage baselines (140 / 70 and 55 / 35 and the rest), so no
factor value has entered any baseline. `fault_standing_interval_share_31f540f0` keeps its tiers
(half, three quarters, rounded down to the nearer hundred) and its worked figures
(9350 → 4600 / 7000 / 9350) with only "the share and the adjustments" replaced by "the additions
and reductions"; `lapsed_registration_image_addition_8c25d3d0` keeps tiers 1 and 2 (4 and 2
images) unchanged and now closes its third clause to "Any other vehicle adds nothing on this
ground, an addition of 0 images", with the point of judgement and the worked reading extended to
say so ("A registration exactly 7 calendar days past expiry is on neither of them and falls to
the third clause"; "A registration 5 calendar days past its expiry … adds nothing on this
ground"). Neither change moves a value in either task.

taken off **the reported stretch** once" — and each is carried verbatim in its own computation
document. The renaming is a source change, not a rendering invention.

`listings_ext_reported_consumption.params` no longer carries `reading_variance_tolerance_miles`;
it carries **`queried_reading_margin_miles: 75`**. That removes the name collision with the base
class parameter `odometer_variance_tolerance_miles`, which survives unchanged in

tier 2 carries the new ladder wording verbatim — source "cut back by the seventy-five mile margin
the marketplace queries rather than charges", document "cut back by the 75 mile margin the
marketplace queries rather than charges", the numeral rendered as a figure as the render contract
requires — and `meta.carries` now reads
